Package com.privatechain.storage.fs

Class FileSystemStorage

java.lang.Object
com.privatechain.storage.fs.FileSystemStorage
All Implemented Interfaces:
BlockchainStorage
public final class FileSystemStorage extends Object implements BlockchainStorage
File system backed BlockchainStorage implementation that stores each block as a separate JSON file.

This implementation has zero native library dependencies, making it suitable for environments where the native LevelDB or RocksDB JNI binaries are unavailable (FR-STOR-05). It relies entirely on the JDK's Files API.

File layout

 <dataDirectory>/
 ├── block-0000000000.json   (genesis block)
 ├── block-0000000001.json
 ├── block-0000000002.json
 └── ...

Each file is named block-%010d.json (10-digit zero-padded decimal index) so that lexicographic file-system ordering matches block order, making loadAll() a simple directory listing without extra sorting on any platform.

Write atomicity

Blocks are written atomically using the write-to-temp-then-rename strategy: the JSON is first written to a .tmp file, then atomically moved over the target via StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE. On POSIX systems this maps to rename(2), which is atomic — readers never see a partial block file.

Stream resource management

Files.list(Path) returns a Stream backed by an open directory-handle. Every call site that opens a directory stream does so inside its own try-with-resources block so the handle is closed immediately after use, regardless of exceptions. No helper method returns an open stream to the caller — this is the pattern recommended by the JDK Javadoc and required to silence static-analysis warnings.

Thread safety

Concurrent reads use the read lock; all writes acquire the exclusive write lock, satisfying FR-STOR-06.

Usage


 BlockchainNode node = BlockchainConfig.builder()
     .storage(new FileSystemStorage("/var/blockchain/chain"))
     .build();

1.0.0

    • FileSystemStorage

      public FileSystemStorage(String dataDirectory)
      Constructs a FileSystemStorage rooted at the given directory path.

      The directory is created (including all missing parents) if it does not already exist.

      Parameters:
      dataDirectory - path to the directory where block files will be stored
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if dataDirectory is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if dataDirectory is blank
      BlockValidationException - if the directory cannot be created

  • Method Details

    • saveBlock

      public void saveBlock(Block block)
      Persists a block as a JSON file using an atomic write-then-rename strategy.
      1. Serialize the block to JSON bytes via BlockSerializer.
      2. Write bytes to block-XXXXXXXXXX.json.tmp.
      3. Atomically rename the temp file to block-XXXXXXXXXX.json.
      Specified by:
      saveBlock in interface BlockchainStorage
      Parameters:
      block - the block to persist (non-null)
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if block is null
      BlockValidationException - if the write or rename fails

    • loadAll

      public List<Block> loadAll()
      Returns all stored blocks in ascending index order.

      Opens a directory stream inside a try-with-resources block to guarantee the underlying directory handle is closed after enumeration.

      The returned list is a defensive copy; mutations do not affect storage.

      Specified by:
      loadAll in interface BlockchainStorage
      Returns:
      non-null, ordered list (maybe empty)

    • deleteAll

      public void deleteAll()
      Deletes all block JSON files from the data directory.

      Warning: irreversible. Only block-*.json files are removed; other files in the directory are untouched.

      Opens a directory stream inside a try-with-resources block to guarantee the underlying directory handle is closed after deletion.
